st.headline: S&P closes at record high as soft jobs report eases rate-hike concerns
st.teaser: The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 151.83 points, or 0.28 per cent, to 54,036.93.
fullText: NEW YORK - US stocks advanced on Aug 7, with the S&P closing at a record high to cap off a strong week of gains for the major indexes, after data showed the US economy unexpectedly shed jobs in July and dampened expectations the Federal Reserve would raise interest rates at its September meeting.
The Labour Department said nonfarm payrolls decreased by 23,000 jobs in July, well below the estimate of economists polled by Reuters that called for an increase of 80,000 jobs.

Previously reported job gains for the prior two months were also revised sharply lower, while the unemployment rate fell to 4.1 per cent in July from 4.2 per cent in June due to workers leaving the labour force.
Market expectations for a rate hike from the Fed at its next meeting dropped to about 44 per cent, according to CME FedWatch, down from 55 per cent in the prior session and 67 per cent a week ago.
Signs of progress for a potential peace deal in the Iran war have helped cool oil prices and, in turn, have eased inflation worries that could prompt a Fed rate hike and pushed Treasury yields lower.

A strong earnings season has also tempered concerns about the massive spending by AI-related companies, sending each of the three major indexes to their biggest weekly percentage gains since mid-April.

“You probably have to lower rates to kind of stimulate job growth, but if you lower rates, you’re going to also stimulate inflation. So you’re kind of in a pickle at this point, and yet the market’s just taken off because earnings have been stellar,” said Tom Siomades, chief market economist at AE Wealth Management in Topeka, Kansas.

“The market should be reacting to weak job numbers and higher inflation and the possibility of a slow-growth economy that may need to have rates raised rather than cut, and yet it’s not. We’re setting records, so go figure.”

With earnings season entering the final stretch, of the 436 companies in the S&P 500 that have already reported results through Friday morning, 85.1 per cent have topped analyst expectations, according to LSEG data – well above the 68 per cent average since 1994.

Under new Fed chairman Kevin Warsh, the US central bank has offered investors little forward guidance on monetary policy, leading market participants to focus on economic data and commentary from policymakers.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 151.83 points, or 0.28 per cent, to 54,036.93, the S&P 500 gained 47.68 points, or 0.62 per cent, to 7,757.64 and the Nasdaq Composite gained 342.26 points, or 1.3 per cent, to 26,690.62.
For the week, the S&P 500 gained 3.58 per cent, the Nasdaq rose 5.19 per cent, and the Dow climbed 2.96 per cent.
Elon Musk’s SpaceX surged 15.8 per cent a day after the expiry of the first of several share lockup restrictions following its record public offering in June.

Collaboration software maker Atlassian shot up 35.3 per cent for its largest-ever daily percentage gain, while chip company Microchip Tech jumped 13.9 per cent, its best daily performance in more than 15 months, after both forecast quarterly revenue above estimates.

Among other movers, vacation rental company Airbnb rose 17.4 per cent as the best performer on the S&P 500 after beating second-quarter revenue estimates. In contrast, Trade Desk plummeted 21.9 per cent as the worst performer on the benchmark index after the ad-tech firm forecast third-quarter revenue below expectations.
Advancing issues outnumbered decliners by a 2.49-to-1 ratio on the New York Stock Exchange and by a 2.07-to-1 ratio on the Nasdaq.
The S&P 500 posted nine new 52-week highs and one new low while the Nasdaq Composite recorded 123 new highs and 77 new lows.
Volume on U.S. exchanges was 16.94 billion shares, compared with the 17.56 billion average for the full session over the last 20 trading days. REUTERS

cna.headline: Flintoff steps down as England Lions coach
cna.teaser: Flintoff steps down as England Lions coach
fullText: Aug 8 : Former England all-rounder Andrew Flintoff has stepped down as head coach of the England Lions, the country's cricket board said on Friday, leaving the 48-year-old to focus on his coaching role at Australia's Sydney Thunder in the Big Bash League.

Flintoff had led England's second-string side since September 2024 and was initially expected to continue in the role alongside his appointment at the Thunder, which was announced in June. He had been due to leave a planned Lions tour of South Africa early to join the Australian franchise.
However, he opted to leave the national setup ahead of the Lions' upcoming assignments, including Pakistan's four-day warm-up match before a three-match test series against England later this month.
"Unfortunately I've made the decision to step away from my role with the Lions," Flintoff said in a statement.
"I can't wait to get started with the Thunder later in the year and see where coaching takes me."
Flintoff also coached Northern Superchargers in The Hundred and worked with England's white-ball teams in an informal consultant capacity before taking charge of the Lions.
The cricket board said Mike Yardy would take charge as the head coach of the Professional County Club Select XI for Pakistan's four-day warm-up match at Beckenham beginning on Tuesday.
A single handpicked story that we think you shouldn't miss. Just one a day.

economistArticle.title: Adapting on the Fly: How India’s Tech Giants are Navigating the Generative AI Wave
paras: For decades, India’s massive information technology (IT) sector has been the engine of its middle-class growth. Millions of young engineering graduates found stable, white-collar jobs writing basic code and maintaining legacy computer systems for global firms. However, the spectacular rise of generative artificial intelligence (AI) has sparked fears of an existential crisis. If large language models can write code in seconds, what becomes of India's army of junior coders?

Yet, early indications suggest that India’s technology giants, from TCS to Infosys, are not merely surviving; they are actively adapting. Instead of wholesale layoffs, these firms are aggressively upskilling their workforces. Programmers are being retrained not just to write code manually, but to act as editors and supervisors of AI-generated output. This shift has redefined the entry-level IT role from rote programming to complex system integration.

Nevertheless, the transition is far from painless for the country's vast pool of fresh graduates. The barrier to entry is rising. Firms that once hired thousands of raw recruits straight from university campuses are now far more discerning. They expect new hires to possess cognitive agility and a rudimentary understanding of machine learning architectures, leaving many average graduates stranded in a hyper-competitive job market.

Crucially, the survival of Indian IT relies on the sheer volume of global demand for digital transformation. Even as AI automates routine tasks, it creates a parallel need for custom enterprise solutions, data curation, and cybersecurity—domains where Indian firms possess formidable scale. By positioning themselves as the ultimate executors of AI integration, these firms aim to prove that artificial intelligence is a tool to be wielded, not a replacement to be feared.
economistArticle.cn: 几十年来，印度庞大的信息技术（IT）行业一直是其中产阶级增长的引擎。数百万年轻工程毕业生在为全球公司编写基础代码和维护传统计算机系统方面找到了稳定的白领工作。然而，生成式人工智能（AI）的惊人崛起引发了人们对其生存危机的担忧。如果大型语言模型能在几秒钟内编写代码，那么印度庞大的初级程序员队伍又将何去何从？然而，早期迹象表明，从塔塔咨询服务（TCS）到印孚瑟斯（Infosys），印度的技术巨头不仅生存了下来，而且正在积极适应。这些公司并没有进行大规模裁员，而是积极提升员工的技能。程序员们正在接受重新培训，不仅要手动编写代码，还要担任AI生成输出的编辑和监督者。这一转变将入门级IT角色从机械式的编程重新定义为复杂的系统集成。然而，对于该国庞大的应届毕业生群体而言，这一过渡远非毫无痛苦。准入门槛正在提高。那些曾经直接从大学校园招收数千名新员工的公司现在变得更加挑剔。他们希望新员工具备认知敏捷性和对机器学习架构的基本了解，这导致许多普通的毕业生在竞争异常激烈的就业市场中陷入困境。关键是，印度IT行业的生存依赖于全球对数字化转型庞大的需求量。即使AI使日常任务实现自动化，它也会创造对定制企业解决方案、数据整理和网络安全等领域的并行需求，而印度公司在这些领域拥有强大的规模。通过将自己定位为AI集成的最终执行者，这些公司旨在证明，人工智能是一个可以利用的工具，而不是一个令人恐惧的替代品。

gems.s: By positioning themselves as the ultimate executors of AI integration, these firms aim to prove that artificial intelligence is a tool to be wielded, not a replacement to be feared.
gems.why: This sentence uses a powerful parallel structure ('a tool to be wielded, not a replacement to be feared') to create contrast and rhetorical balance, showing advanced persuasive writing. 这个句子采用了强有力的平行/对比结构（‘一个可以利用的工具，而不是一个令人恐惧的替代品’）来创造对比和修辞平衡，展示了高级的劝说性写作技巧。
